description: The gate that decides whether a research batch is actually finished
---

Never claim a batch is done from your own reading of it. Run the gate the
SessionStart contract names:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/adversarial_pass_audit.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/search_log_completeness.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
```

The second line is RC4 (advisory): it FAILs if this session wrote to any of the 2026-08-19
RULE's research tables and no closed adversarial pass names it. That FAIL is not a reason to
close pass 1; LED-192 holds it open (`/adversarial` step 3). Run it on `CURRENT`, not via
`run_checks.py --battery research` — that battery's other session-scoped checks
(`research_dod_session`, `author_fidelity`, `citation_mining_session`) are still pointed
at `LATEST-RESEARCH`, which names the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of this one.

The third line is I5, also on `CURRENT`: it reads the WebSearch/WebFetch ledger the
harness hook wrote and FAILs a WebSearch query that no `search_executions.query_text` of
this session contains — a search you ran and did not log (R8). Log it with
`db.py log-search --backfill 1`: the row is a reconstruction, not a log made as the search
ran, and the `--prior-expectation` it still requires is written after the results, so it
is post hoc and must say so. Its REPORTED lines (unpersisted WebFetch URLs, bare curl/wget
hosts, and web rows logged with no web line on the ledger — a hook that may not have
fired) belong in the session record; they do not fail, and a NOTHING-IN-SCOPE verdict does
not clear them. It witnesses WebSearch and WebFetch only: a search run through an MCP tool
(Consensus, PubMed, Scholar Gateway) leaves no line, so a PASS says nothing about those. R8 still
owes each of them a `log-search` row, and `record_file` its result (DR-2026-09-26 §2.2b); the
gate can check neither.

**The session id is the bare stem in the DB and carries `.md` in pointer files.**
Wrong form scopes the gate to zero rows and every rule reports PASS over an empty
subject — green, and meaningless.

If it fails, the batch is not done. Fix the rows, re-emit, re-run. Do not
baseline the failure away: `governance/research-contract-baseline.json` ratchets
DOWN only, and raising a count there forgives fresh violations invisibly.

When it passes, confirm the corpus posture has not regressed:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --all
```

Then commit the scratchpad and the agent transcripts (`scripts/preserve_transcripts.py`)
— a read-only subagent writes nothing at all, so its entire workings live in
ephemeral container storage until they are copied out.

Then gate the diff once, when the batch is ready to open a PR: `scripts/preflight.sh`
(CLAUDE.md §1) — not `run_checks.py --all`.

# T-079  A deferred reading is recorded, and every deferred act lists with its age from one view
_One task, one pull request. Read `CLAUDE.md` first; beyond it this file is self-contained. Index, order and the owner decision register: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`. Source: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/OPEN-ITEMS-PLAN.md` row OI-56 (AT-17), probe in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/pilot/R2-probes.md` (section AT-17). Every number in this file was read on 2026-11-13 on commit `66a5ba8a` and is given with the command that produces it: re-run the command; do not trust the number._
**Pilot status.** Not piloted. Authored 2026-11-13; the R2 probe was re-run on that day's HEAD. Expect to find a defect in this file, and report it rather than work around it.
## 1. Identity
| | |
|---|---|
| Task | T-079 |
| Title | A deferred reading is recorded, and every deferred act lists with its age from one view |
| Wave | 2 |
| Layer (CLAUDE.md §3) | 1-2 |
| Kind | **TOOLING** (CLAUDE.md rule 10: tooling and research never share a pull request) |
| Executor | Sonnet-class |
| Traces to | AT-17 ("The set of deferred acts (mining, searches, readings) older than a stated age can be listed by one query", `grep -n 'AT-17' scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/td-requirements-and-interface-spec.md`); REQ-036; the owner's "deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually" (`grep -n -F 'deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually' references/project-standards.md`) and the ledger's own finding beneath it that "nothing in this repository enforces it or even measures it" |
## 2. Preconditions
- **The integration base.** `origin/main` once the workplan's pull request is merged, otherwise the remote branch carrying the newest commit to this folder (the set-up block's first line finds it).
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** none.
- **Owner decisions:** none. The ruling is the owner's (2026-09-18): a deferral is legitimate "so long as it runs eventually", and for mining "the execution signal already exists and it is `evidence_sources.citation_mining_status`" (`grep -n -F 'The execution signal already exists' references/project-standards.md`). Extending the record to readings is AT-17's reading of REQ-036 ("by extension every owed act"); it adds no doctrine: a deferred reading is still owed, and the scan ledger still lists the pair as unread.
- **Tests that must be red before you start:** AT-17, restated in section 6.
- **Set-up.**
git fetch origin
W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1); echo "BASE=$BASE"
git switch -c task/t-079-deferred-acts-with-age "$BASE"              # real execution only
sha256sum data/guidebook.db
export SCRATCH="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guidebook-t-079" && mkdir -p "$SCRATCH" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/t.db"
```
- Shell variables do not survive between tool calls: begin every later block with the `W=…; BASE=…` and `export SCRATCH=…` lines. **Real execution:** `/session-open` first. **Pilot:** no `/session-open`, stay on the given branch, stop after section 7.
## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms
A deferred act is a promise to go back: a search not run, a source not mined, a source not read. The owner allows deferral on the condition that the act eventually runs. Searches and mining record their deferrals with a date; a reading has no deferred state at all, so "we chose not to read this yet" cannot be told from "nobody has looked", and no query lists all three with their age. A deferral that is never discharged is indistinguishable from one taken last week.
**Evidence commands** (read-only):
```
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True)
print('search deferrals', c.execute("select count(*) from search_executions where deferred_reason is not null").fetchone()[0])
print('mining deferrals standing', c.execute("select count(*) from citation_mining cm join evidence_sources e on e.ref_id=coalesce(cm.global_ref_id,cm.local_ref_id) where cm.deferred_reason is not null and e.citation_mining_status='deferred'").fetchone()[0])
print('source_scans columns with defer/status', [r[1] for r in c.execute('pragma table_info(source_scans)') if 'defer' in r[1] or 'status' in r[1]])
print('v_scan_ledger columns', [r[1] for r in c.execute('pragma table_info(v_scan_ledger)')])
print('ledger statuses', c.execute('select status,count(*) from v_scan_ledger group by 1').fetchall())
print('views over deferrals', [r[0] for r in c.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='view' and name like '%defer%'")])
PY
```
**Output on 2026-11-13:** `search deferrals 1`; `mining deferrals standing 13`; `source_scans columns with defer/status []`; `v_scan_ledger columns ['ref_id', 'parameter_id', 'status', 'scan_id', 'text_scope', 'method']` (no date); statuses `EXTRACTED`, `NOT-READ`, `READ-NOTHING-FOUND`, `READ-PARTIAL`, `STATED-ABSENT` (no deferred one); `views over deferrals []`. A union over searches and mining with an age filter runs today (the R2 probe's), but a reading cannot enter it.
If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9).
## 4. The change
Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.
1. **Schema migration: a table `reading_deferrals`** (`deferral_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, `ref_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id)`, `parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id)` (NULL: the whole-source catalogue reading), `reason TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (trim(reason) <> '')`, `created_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `created_by_session TEXT NOT NULL`). Add it to `governance/stage-map.yaml` as `evidence` (beside `source_scans`, which the map puts there: `grep -n 'source_scans' governance/stage-map.yaml`).
   **Chosen (authoring 2026-11-13):** a table of its own. Rejected: (a) a row in `source_scans` (its `file_sha256 NOT NULL` and `text_scope` describe a reading that happened; a deferral is the opposite fact); (b) `evidence_sources.data_capture_status = 'deferred'` (per source only, no date and no reason, and a column a data migration INSERTs, CLAUDE.md rule 5); (c) a new `v_scan_ledger` status (the pair stays owed until it is read, and the gates that read the ledger's statuses would change meaning). The deferral is **discharged by derivation, never by a write**: a `full` reading in `source_scans` that covers the pair (catalogue mode with `catalogue_version >= parameter_id`, or targeted at it; for a NULL parameter, any full catalogue reading of the source) and is dated after the deferral.
2. **`db.py defer-reading --ref-id R [--parameter P] --reason TEXT --session S`.** Refuses: a source that does not exist or is superseded (`superseded_by_ref_id IS NOT NULL`: the replacement is what is owed); a parameter that is not active; a blank reason; a pair a full reading already covers (nothing is owed); a pair that already has an undischarged deferral. Reuse the existing helpers for each (`_parameter_row`, `dbcore.require_reason`, the source lookups `record-scan` uses, including its tombstone refusal `_refuse_tombstone`: `grep -n 'def record_scan' -A60 scripts/db.py`).
3. **A view `v_deferred_acts`** with columns `kind` (`search`, `mining`, `reading`), `subject` (the exec id; the mined `ref_id` and slug; the `ref_id` and parameter), `reason`, `deferred_at`, `created_by_session`, listing **only standing deferrals**:
   - searches: `search_executions` with `deferred_reason IS NOT NULL`, dated `created_at`. A deferred search has no discharge pointer today (a search later run is a new row that names nothing it discharges), so every search deferral lists; say so in the view's header comment.
   - mining: `citation_mining` rows with `deferred_reason IS NOT NULL` whose source's `citation_mining_status` is still `deferred` (the owner's home for the execution signal), dated `citation_mining.created_at`.
   - readings: `reading_deferrals` with no discharging reading (item 1).
   **Chosen (authoring 2026-11-13):** the date is when the obligation was first recorded (`created_at`), not when the row was last written (`updated_at`): a re-deferral that reset the clock would hide an old obligation, the failure the 2026-09-18 entry names. The age query AT-17 asks for is then `select * from v_deferred_acts where deferred_at < datetime('now', '-<N> days')`; no age threshold is stored or typed anywhere (rule 7a). The view reads three stages beyond base (research for searches and mining, evidence for sources and readings): it is a cross-stage pointer view (CLAUDE.md §3); name the stages in its header comment.
4. **Nothing reads the view as a gate in this task.** It is the measure the 2026-09-18 entry says is missing; a check that fails on an aged deferral would need an age the owner has not set (section 9 of this file names that as an owner question, not this task's).
**Schema migration (this task has one).** Never type a migration number: `ls scripts/migrations | grep -E '^[0-9]{3}_' | sort | tail -1` gives the highest; yours is that plus one, in `scripts/migrations/NNN_reading_deferrals.sql`, ending with `PRAGMA user_version` set to the same number. Apply only with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py`; prove with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild "$SCRATCH/rebuilt.db"` (exit 0) and `python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --deep` (PASS). Run `python3 scripts/audit/joined_cells_census.py` before and after (no new candidate). A new table must be writable by the capture path: confirm `reading_deferrals` appears in `dbcore.writable_tables(conn)` on the migrated copy (it is derived from the INSERTs in `db.py`; `python3 -I -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import dbcore,sqlite3;print('reading_deferrals' in dbcore.writable_tables(sql
**What reads what this task adds:** a session or the owner asking which promises are outstanding and how old; `/orient` may read the view later (not changed here); the R6 rule of `research_dod` (deferral is not a findings channel) is unaffected. **What it makes deletable:** the hand-written union a reader would otherwise write each time.
**Code size.** Report `git diff --shortstat "$(git merge-base HEAD "$BASE")" -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` after `git add`, and name what reads each addition.
## 5. Caller sweep
Names to sweep: `deferred_reason`, `citation_mining_status`, `source_scans`, `v_scan_ledger`, `writable_tables`.
**What a caller is.** A hit is a *caller* when its behaviour or its truth changes with this task (code, a test, a view, a registry entry, a skill or governance sentence that says a reading cannot be deferred, or that lists the deferral homes). A mention stays true. Fixing a caller is in scope (CLAUDE.md rule 4). Left out: `workplan/`, `references/project-standards.md`, `scripts/migrations/`, `sessions/`, `_archived/`, `audits/`, `versions/`, `transcripts/`, `scratchpad/`.

## 6. Verification
**Step 1, before any edit: the before-run.**
```

for c in $CHECKS; do cmd=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys,shlex;print(shlex.join(next(x['cmd'] for x in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/check-registry.yaml'))['checks'] if x['id']==sys.argv[1])))" $c); $cmd > "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt" 2>&1; echo "$c rc=$? | $(grep -E '^ *EXAMINED:|RESULTS|FAILED|VERDICT' "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt" | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-200)"; done
```
Red here on 2026-11-13: `test_scan_contract` (G01, G02), `scan_debt`, `research_dod` (R12): record and carry on.
**Step 2: red before, green after** (cases `T079-01`… in `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py`; prefix free: `git grep -c 'T079-' scripts/tests/`):
- `T079-01` AT-17: on a scratch copy, defer one reading through the verb (a source and an active parameter chosen by query, a pair whose ledger status is `NOT-READ`: `select ref_id, parameter_id from v_scan_ledger where status='NOT-READ' order by 1,2 limit 1`); then `select kind, count(*) from v_deferred_acts group by kind` returns all three kinds, and the age query with a window that excludes today returns the older search and mining rows and not the new reading. Red before (no table, no verb, no view; assert stderr starts `REFUSING:` or the verb is unknown).
- `T079-02` refusals: blank reason; superseded source; inactive parameter; a pair already covered by a full reading (build one with `db.py record-scan` on the copy); a second undischarged deferral of the same pair.
- `T079-03` discharge: record a full catalogue reading of the deferred source on the copy (`db.py record-scan`, `TASK-FIXTURE` notes) and the deferral leaves the view; a `partial` reading does not discharge it.
- `T079-04` mining: on the copy, discharge one standing mining deferral with `log-mining --discharge-deferral` and it leaves the view.

**Step 4: the gate, once.**

3c575c89c1a6af4b9d2192e9eb43ed78bfeb366d7b31fe5fe41715c731634cdb  data/guidebook.db
CREATE TABLE term_adjudications (
    adjudication_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    observation_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    -- OUTCOMES, documented HERE and not inside the CHECK. dbcore.check_values() reads
    -- this constraint's own value list to build the CLI's refusal, and an inline
    -- comment between the quoted values defeats its parser -- measured 2026-09-03,
    -- when a first cut of this migration carried the descriptions inside the IN(...)
    -- and every legitimate outcome was refused with a mangled vocabulary. The whole
    -- reason vocabularies come from the schema rather than a list in the code
    -- (CLAUDE.md §4) is defeated by punctuation the parser cannot see past.
    --
    --   NAMES-EXISTING  names a term we already hold
    --   NAMES-NEW       names a concept new to the vocabulary
    --   NOT-OURS        a real phrase, but not one of our concepts
    --   DEFERRED        cannot be settled on this source alone
    outcome             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN
                            ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW','NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')),
    term_id             TEXT REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    -- NOT NULL: an adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested, and the
    -- whole point of splitting observation from judgment is that the judgement is
    -- inspectable.
    rationale           TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    -- The outcome and the pointer must agree. An outcome that names a term must name
    -- one; an outcome that declines must not.
    CHECK (
        (outcome IN ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW') AND term_id IS NOT NULL)
     OR (outcome IN ('NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')        AND term_id IS NULL)
    )
)

      every extraction in the database was filed under the one parameter that existed, and

DESIGN RULES for anyone extending this gate (learned by attacking it on 2026-07-24, when eight
    # R16: a term NAMED by an adjudication of those observations that holds neither a
    # parameter (base_parameters, any status: a merged or retired parameter is a recorded
    # decision about the term) nor a declination (parameter_declinations, migration 101).
    # `a.term_id IS NOT NULL` is the schema's own pairing CHECK for the outcomes that name a
    # term, so the outcome vocabulary stays out of this file (CLAUDE.md rule 8) and
    # NAMES-EXISTING counts as well as NAMES-NEW: a phrase naming a term we already hold is
    # still a concept the source states a figure for. Every named term can be disposed of by
    # one call, add-parameter or decline-parameter, and neither refuses for want of anything
    # this batch must first do, so the rule does not hold red a batch that did its judging.
    # ONE EXCEPTION, stated rather than discovered: add-parameter refuses a term whose
    # canonical_en carries a value (db.py _VALUE_BEARING) and canonical_en has no amend
    # path, so such a term could be disposed of only by a declination that would be untrue.
    # add-term refuses those names, and no live term carries one; re-derive by matching
    # `select canonical_en from terms` against _VALUE_BEARING. Meeting one is a GAP to file.
    # THE PREDICATE IS WIDER THAN THE RULE'S TITLE. Nothing here can tell whether a source
    # states a figure for a named concept, so every named term must be disposed of, figure
    # or none. A disposition is per term and corpus-wide, so that costs one call per term
    # once, not one per batch.
    # WHAT THIS DOES NOT TEST, stated so the PASS line is not "strengthened": a figure stated
    # for a concept no observation records leaves no row here, and whether a parameter goes
    # on to carry an extraction is not read either.
    adj_join = ("FROM term_adjudications a "
                "JOIN observed_terms o ON o.observation_id = a.observation_id "
                "JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = o.ref_id ")
    # A REVOKED declination (migration 104, `db.py revoke-declination`) disposes of nothing:
    # someone decided the term may be a parameter after all, so it is owed a disposition
    # again. The row stays as history; this predicate reads it as absent.
    undisposed = _rows(cx,
        "SELECT DISTINCT a.term_id " + adj_join +
        "WHERE a.term_id IS NOT NULL "
        "AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM base_parameters p WHERE p.term_id = a.term_id) "
        "AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM parameter_declinations d WHERE d.term_id = a.term_id "
        "AND d.revoked_at IS NULL)"
        + escope + " ORDER BY a.term_id", sargs)
    n_named = _rows(cx, "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.term_id) " + adj_join +

    # The outcomes that name no term, grouped from the rows rather than listed here.
    unnamed = _rows(cx, "SELECT a.outcome, COUNT(*) " + adj_join +

                    "ORDER BY a.outcome", sargs)

## 2. Preconditions

- **The integration base.** This workplan must be on the branch you start from. If the workplan's pull request is merged, that is `origin/main`. Until then it is the workplan branch, `origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0` (if that name is gone: `git branch -r --contains "$(git log --all --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md)"`). Every command in this file uses `$BASE`, set by the first line of the set-up block, and never a literal `origin/main`: on a base that lacks the workplan, a diff against `origin/main` contains the whole workplan and every gate and count is about the wrong change.
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** T-019 merged. Check by running that task's own after-test (its section 6), or `git log "$BASE" --oneline | grep -F "<that task's commit subject>"`.
- **Owner decisions:** none outstanding. The decisions this task needed are resolved under delegation (next bullet); none is still the owner's.
- **Delegated resolutions this task rests on.** OD-06: judgment assigns the lens codes, from the full reading; evidence assigns none. (The mobility codes are not this task's: OD-14, the owner's, through T-102.) Each is a resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12: not the owner's words, reversible by the owner, and read only through the ledger's gate (`grep -n -F "Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution" references/project-standards.md`). Run it before you start and again before you open the pull request; if any line prints CLOSED, stop and report: a CLOSED gate is a stop like those of section 9.
```
gate(){ s=$(grep -F "$1 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); c=$(grep -F "$1 CHECK:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); case "$s" in *"ANSWERED BY THE OWNER"*) echo "$1 OPEN (owner)";; *"RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"*) case "$c" in *"not required"*|*confirmed*) echo "$1 OPEN (delegated; ${c#*CHECK: })";; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (check: ${c:-none})";; esac;; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (${s:-no status line})";; esac; }
for n in OD-06; do gate $n; done
```
## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. Per D-2: fill a lens only where a quote names the users. Each lens is a link row written with `db.py add-lens-link --extraction-id N --icf|--needs|--medical <code> --basis named_in_text --basis-text "<the words>"` (`T-018-design.md` section 6); a judged link replaces a `carried` one in the same call. Judgment assigns the lenses (OD-06, resolved under delegation; owner 2026-08-27, the deep read is judgment's). Do not tag an identity code of the mobility family here (`MOB`, or a child T-102 adds: `WHEEL`, `LLD`, `WALKAID`, as revised by the owner on 2026-11-12, sixth to ninth sets), nor `SCI`, `LMB` or `UPL` (retired to `WHEEL` by T-102, and to `UPL` by T-116): the identity carrying is those tasks'. **Do** fill the ICF (d4) and needs lenses of figures on `MOB` where the quote names the function or need: a figure that names no group stays on the parent `MOB` under T-102, and these lenses are what then make it findable (OD-14 answered 2026-11-12). Do not write a device into `device_class` as a stand-in for an identity tag.

**What reads what this task adds or changes:** the engine

**Data migration.** This task lands rows through `scripts/emit_data_migration.py`, which names the file itself; never type a migration name or number, and never edit the file it writes. The pull request contains no schema migration and no file under `scripts/` other than that one `scripts/migrations/data_*` file.

## 5. Caller sweep
- **Owner decisions:** none in the register. Rulings: OR-13 ("From the codes held": the quantities are seeded by an open-pass scan of the codes already held, not slug by slug); OR-17 (the assistant approves vocabulary in bulk; the owner reads the pull request; no phrase the model generated); E1 (a concept first met outside English is named by the instrument's own phrase, in its own language, until an English-language instrument of the scope names it; no English gloss typed); E12 (the functional-axis and method terms are declined as parameters). **One gate already stated elsewhere holds part of this task:** a parameter whose quantity kind is not yet in `base_quantity_kinds` waits for the owner to approve the new kind in a dated ledger entry (T-109 section 4 item 1: "a new kind is proposed with its warrant for the add-kind verb, never typed into a cell"). This task proposes such kinds in a table; it does not add them.

## Owner answers 2026-11-13 (tenth set) — the T-4 agreement rules (OR-5b, OR-6c), the floor marker and the code route (OR-22b, OR-23b), element pages (OR-14b), scan batches (OR-25), the term "barrier-free path of travel" (OT-2), the order of the three criteria (OI-14), and the mobility family's crossings, SCI edge, wording and edges (OI-03, OI-48, OI-49, OI-50)

Given in the session that opened from PR #219, in reply to the prompts of `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/OPEN-ITEMS-PLAN.md` section 6 asked one by one with their context (the context text is the owner queue's own, `governance/owner-browser.yaml`). Dated by the server clock, UTC. Each answer is the owner's selected option or typed words, quoted; a reading by the assistant is marked [ASSUMPTION] and is not the owner's.

**OR-5b — how a Co-1 source is shown to be academically sound.** The owner first answered with a link only: "https://equator-network.org/". The assistant read that as conformity to the reporting guideline for the source's design, and asked. The owner replied:

> "Yes, PRISM for systematic reviews/meta-analyses, academic rigour re PubMed for any other study outside those bounds, and then ISO for T4-6 as relevant"

[ASSUMPTION: "PRISM" is PRISMA, the EQUATOR reporting guideline for systematic reviews and meta-analyses — the spelling differs; unratified.] [ASSUMPTION: "ISO for T4-6 as relevant" means the standards body's own instrument (an ISO or national standard) is the test for the regulatory stratum; unratified.] **What it does not decide.** (1) What "academic rigour re PubMed" means: indexed in PubMed, or judged by the standard PubMed-indexed work meets. The two differ, and the first collides with the research contract's R5 ("Non-English peer-reviewed work is ACADEMIC, not grey. Non-indexation in PubMed/Scopus is an INDEXING fact, not an evidence-quality fact"). The assistant does not choose between them. (2) How a DPO position statement or a lived-experience publication, which has no reporting guideline and is not a study in the sense of the second clause, is shown to be sound. The assistant had stated that by a guideline test such a source would set direction only; the reply does not confirm or reverse that. (3) Whether the three-part test is for Co-1 only or for every tier's soundness. T-4 step 3 asks the owner these three before it builds the field and verb.

OR-5b STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER, PARTLY (the test is named; its three edges above are open)

**OR-6c — how far "the T1 figure is stated, the T2 dispute noted" reaches.** The owner selected "Any different tiers" and added: "Co-1 and T1 are same value". The assistant read this as one rank for Co-1 and T1 and asked; the owner answered "Yes, both (1) and (2)":

> (1) Co-1 against T2 (or lower): the Co-1 figure is stated and the T2 dispute noted, as for T1; (2) Co-1 against T1: same rank, so neither is stated over the other, and the divergence waits for an approach written by an Opus-class session (the same applies to two sources of the same tier).

The design range is unchanged (the OR-6c prompt's stated default; the owner did not alter it).
OR-6c STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OR-22b — the marker of a floor claim a study confirms by absence.** Selected: "The study's own band". The cell reads the band of the verified, retrieved study that confirmed it; migration 116's regulation-only rule (○) does not apply to it.
OR-22b STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OR-23b — whether a registry citation is a valid route for an unretrievable code or standard.** Selected: "Yes, for T4 to T6". An unretrievable code or standard keeps its tier and may anchor below the weak band when cited by jurisdiction, standard number and clause; the academic route is still required of the other kinds of source.
OR-23b STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OR-14b — who writes an element page.** Selected: "Written by the pass". The specifications pass writes an element-level determination from the related parameters' determinations. **Effect:** a new stage output (a table and a rule version) built in a tooling pull request; it ends the deferral of cross-parameter synthesis tables (R17) for the element case. The element is still never a container that figures are filed into. The plan has no task for this (T-037 stops on OR-14b; the element pointer was mapped to T-029 on the derived-at-read basis); the coordinating session files one.
OR-14b STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OR-25 — whether batch 23's extraction cap carries over to scans.** Selected: "No cap; one source (Recommended)". Ratifies the 2026-10-09 recommendation: one source is the review unit; D-3 and T-105 batch by source.
OR-25 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OT-2 — the term "barrier-free path of travel".** Selected: "Approve" the drafted definition and scope note as shown in the owner queue (`governance/owner-browser.yaml`, OT-2). A data pull request mints the term from observation 68 with `db.py add-term`, citing this answer; observation 71 is untouched and waits on its own prompt.
OT-2 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OI-14 — the order of the three criteria.** Selected: "Yes: 1, then 2, then 3". This ratifies, from this date, the assumption in the delegation entry (2026-11-12) that integrity, rigour and provenance come before legibility, which comes before coverage. It is a new line; the delegation entry is not edited. It is not retroactive in effect: decisions already resolved on that order stand as resolved.
OI-14 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OI-03 — the mobility children's ICF crossings.** Selected: "Yes, as proposed": `WHEEL` to d465, d420, d410 (beside the `SCI` crossings T-102 judges to hold for wheelchair users); `LLD` to d450, d455; `WALKAID` to d450, d465 (moderate, contextual), as in `tasks/T-102-design.md` sections 6a and 7. T-102 writes them with the stated confidence and mechanism.
OI-03 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OI-48 — the `SCI` edge.** Selected: "Accept". A person with an incomplete spinal cord injury who walks is placed by aid (`WALKAID`, or `MOB` with ICF d450/d455), never under `WHEEL`; the injury and its level are held in the medical lens and ICF b-codes; `SCI` has no identity code of its own.
OI-48 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OI-49 — the wording of `UPL` and `LLD`.** Selected: "Confirm both". `UPL`: display name "people with upper-limb differences or disabilities", category `general`. `LLD`: description "People with a lower-limb difference, from limb loss or from birth, whether or not they use a prosthesis. The prosthesis, where a figure concerns one, is recorded on the figure, never as a code."
OI-49 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

**OI-50 — the edges of `UPL` and `LLD`.** Selected: "Confirm both" of (a) and (b): (a) an upper-limb prosthesis user is `UPL`, a lower-limb one is `LLD` with the prosthesis named in `device_class`; (b) the identity codes are not mutually exclusive, so a person with a lower-limb difference who uses a wheelchair is `LLD` and `WHEEL`. (c), whether `UPL` has children, was not asked and none is invented. This ratifies the two [ASSUMPTION] marks of the eighth and ninth sets.
OI-50 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

CONDITION: any session building the T-4 agreement task, writing a determination's marker or value, tagging or crossing a mobility figure, minting or rewording `UPL`, `LLD`, `WHEEL` or `WALKAID`, building an element page, batching a scan, or minting "barrier-free path of travel".
ACTION: (1) T-4: ask the three open edges of OR-5b first; build the divergence rule as OR-6c states it (higher tier states and the lower tier's dispute is noted; Co-1 and T1 are one rank, and a same-rank divergence waits for an Opus-class approach). (2) OR-22b: a floor claim confirmed by absence reads the confirming study's band. (3) OR-23b: a registry citation is a valid route for T4 to T6 only. (4) OR-14b: file the element-determination tooling task; T-037 builds no element page until it has merged. (5) OR-25: batch scans by source. (6) T-102 writes the OI-03 crossings; T-116 and T-025 use the OI-49 wording. (7) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] marks above as unratified, and the two [ASSUMPTION] marks of the eighth and ninth sets as ratified by OI-50. This supersedes, for the element case only, the R17 deferral of cross-parameter synthesis tables.
DATE: 2026-11-13 — owner answers (selected options, and typed words where quoted), above.

## The link table for a figure's lens codes — what OD-39 and OR-1c let T-018 build (migration 131)

On the owner's answer to OD-39 (`grep -n -F "OD-39: the 2026-11-06 link-table ruling supersedes" references/project-standards.md`), the link-table ruling of 2026-11-06 (OR-1c: *"link table unless that is more prone to errors"*) supersedes the clause of the 2026-08-28 ACTION that forbade a `population_*` link table. The owner's words carry no scope: *"Yes, the 2026-11-06 ruling supersedes that clause"*. T-018 builds `extraction_lens_links`, one row per (figure, lens code), and `v_live_lens_links` as the one read surface. The recorder's correction of 2026-11-12 (`grep -n -F "Correction 2026-11-12 — to the fifth set" references/project-standards.md`) explains why this is a prose entry and carries no machine `SUPERSEDES` pair: the audit cannot anchor a target that is itself in this ledger.

**[ASSUMPTION: the supersession is read as covering a figure's lens codes only, not `specifications` or any other table that carries lens columns — the owner's answer names no table; the reading follows OR-1c's own subject, which is the figure ("several codes of one model on a figure"). Unratified; if the owner means a wider reading, every table in the command below is in question.]**

**[ASSUMPTION: the rest of the 2026-08-28 ACTION is read as standing where D-0182 left it — four typed lens columns with real foreign keys, the lens names in the name (no `population`), `population_code` retired in favour of the four — because OD-39 names only the `population_*` link-table clause. Unratified.]** The clause "Never two lenses in one row" does NOT stand as a ruling: D-0182 (owner 2026-09-01, the entry headed "The lens CHECK is at least one, not exactly one", `grep -n -F "overturned that clause" references/project-standards.md`) overturned it, holding that *"a link MUST be tied to at least one"* and *"ideally it ties into many"*. A link row of `extraction_lens_links` states exactly one code by a CHECK. That is T-018's design choice for a new table (it keeps every lens a typed foreign key), not a restoration of the 2026-08-28 clause.

**An open reading of OR-1c, not a settled one.** The owner's decision sheet asked about a figure or a determination. T-018 builds the link table for figures only, and a determination's cell stays a key with one code per model. Whether the link table should cover determinations too is unanswered (OI-55 in the open-items plan). Nothing in this entry decides it.

The figure's own four lens columns are no longer a home for its lens: migration 131 carries every value into `extraction_lens_links` as a `carried` link (count them with `select count(*), count(distinct extraction_id) from extraction_lens_links where basis='carried'`: one row per value, so more rows than figures where a figure holds several), holds the columns NULL by CHECK, and does not drop them because committed data migrations INSERT them. D-0182's rule that a link be tied to at least one lens now lives in the writers and in the blocking `test_db_integrity` case T018-05, not in a CHECK on the figure.

The tables that carry lens columns are derived, never listed here: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);L={'identity_code','icf_code','needs_code','medical_code'};print([(t,[x for x in (r[1] for r in c.execute(f'pragma table_info(\"{t}\")')) if x in L]) for (t,) in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")])"`, keeping those whose list is non-empty. Under the reading above, only `source_value_extractions` (now held NULL) moved to links.

CONDITION: any session asking whether a figure may carry several codes of one lens model, whether a `population_*` link table is forbidden, where a figure's lens lives, whether determinations take a link table, or writing or capturing an `INSERT` that names a lens column of `source_value_extractions`.
ACTION: (1) Read a figure's lens from `v_live_lens_links`, never from the four columns on `source_value_extractions`. (2) Write it with `add-extraction` / `derive-extraction` (repeat the lens flag; `--lens-basis` and `--lens-basis-text` are required) and `add-lens-link` / `retire-lens-link`. (3) A research batch captured before migration 131 merged, and merged after it, holds an `INSERT` of a lens column that the table's CHECK refuses; capture it again through those verbs. (4) Treat the two [ASSUMPTION] marks above as unratified, and the determination question as open.
DATE: 2026-11-13 — recorded by the T-018 executor on the owner's answer to OD-39; not itself an owner statement.

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

Some stored ramp-gradient figures are written `1:12` with the unit cell holding only `ratio`. The engine reads an `a:b` figure only under `rise:run ratio` (rise over horizontal run: a gradient), so it leaves these out of the value and lists them in the cell's note as "no parsable numeric bound". `ratio` alone does not say which run is meant, and whether filling that in is a reformat of the stored row or a new reading of the source is the owner's question OD-41.

## 6. Verification

**The after-test, by answer** (run on `$SCRATCH/t.db` before the work, on `$SCRATCH/s.db` after it, then on the canonical database after the migration):
- (a): `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3,sys;print(sqlite3.connect('file:'+sys.argv[1]+'?mode=ro',uri=True).execute(\"select group_concat(extraction_id) from source_value_extractions where claimed_unit='ratio'\").fetchone()[0])" <db>` prints `None`, or only the ids section 4 item 0 left with a reason. **Red before:** it prints section 3's ids.
- (b): `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3,sys;c=sqlite3.connect('file:'+sys.argv[1]+'?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute(\"select o.extraction_id, count(n.extraction_id) from source_value_extractions o left join source_value_extractions n on n.ref_id=o.ref_id and n.parameter_id=o.parameter_id and n.claim_text=o.claim_text and n.claimed_value=o.claimed_value and n.claimed_unit='rise:run ratio' where o.claimed_unit='ratio' group by 1 having count(n.extraction_id)<>1\").fetchall())" <db>` prints `[]`, or only the ids left with a reason (each stored row has exactly one new reading). **Red before:** it prints every id with count 0.

Report which.

## 7. Commit

Commit **after** the gate of section 6 is clean.
```
git add -A . ':!transcripts' ':!*commands.jsonl'
git commit -m "run-pipeline: the stored ramp gradients whose unit says only ratio, under OD-41 [$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')]" -m "<body: OD-41's answer and its ledger line; the rows, each with the source sentence that shows a horizontal run; rows left and why; the engine's value_note before and after>" -m "<the attribution trailers your own session instructions give>"
```

## 8. What you must NOT do

- Do not start before OD-41 is answered, and do not do the other answer's part.
- Do not change a digit, a quote or a locator. Do not retire, supersede or delete a stored row (OQ-T086).
- Do not build the follow-up branch of T-061 here (tooling, rule 10).
- Do not write `data/guidebook.db` directly; do not hand-write SQL against a table a `db.py` verb can reach.
- Do not decide doctrine; do not treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code as a container. Do not run `scripts/run_checks.py --all`, `scripts/bootstrap.sh` or `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Do not push to `main`, rebase or force-push; do not subscribe to pull-request activity.
- Do not hand-type a count into any file or message; write the command that computes it.

## 9. Stop conditions

Stop, change nothing further, and report when: OD-41 is unanswered, or answered in a form neither (a) nor (b) describes; under (a), the precondition's dry run is refused (the follow-up branch is not merged); under (b), the owner's answer does not say what becomes of the stored row and the engine's report counts both (OQ-T086: ask); section 3's command prints a row that is not `a:b`, or a parameter other than one, or a live determination; a row's source does not show a horizontal run (leave it, list it with the sentence); a check green in the before-run is red after; the rebuild does not reproduce the database; you would have to guess a value, a unit or the owner's intent.

## 10. Rollback

Before the migration is applied: delete the scratch copy; nothing has changed. After it is committed: a data migration is append-only and immutable; correct a wrong row with a compensating migration written through the same verbs, never by editing or deleting the file.

## 11. Adversarial pass and pull request

Real execution only; a pilot stops after section 7. `/adversarial` once on the finished diff (for a research task the pass is recorded with `db.py record-adversarial-pass` and closed with `close-adversarial-pass`); `/batch-done`; push; open the pull request last, once, against the integration base; call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for it immediately; push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change, never `[skip ci]` on the final push.

{'between', '>', '=', '<', '<=', '>=', 'approx'}
CREATE TABLE extraction_relations (
  relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

  -- THE FIGURE THIS EDGE QUALIFIES. NOT NULL and a real FK -- an edge naming no source
  -- row describes nothing. No UNIQUE index touches this column alone: one extraction may
  -- carry several comparator edges (a ramp slope is both condition_on a run-length limit
  -- AND audited_against a code's stated maximum), and collapsing that to one row per
  -- extraction would force a choice this table exists to avoid forcing.
  from_extraction_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),

  -- WHAT KIND OF COMPARISON THIS EDGE IS. Eight values; the CHECK is the vocabulary
  -- (CLAUDE.md section 4) and this is only its meaning, one line each.
  --   tested_at        -- the source physically measured its subjects at/against this
  --                      referent -- REF-00973's four ramp slopes were each tested_at a
  --                      named gradient.
  --   audited_against  -- the source measured whether subjects could perform WITHIN a
  --                      referent's own stated limit, rather than measuring an
  --                      independent value -- REF-00971's "existing standards".
  --   confirms         -- an independent measurement agrees with the referent's value.

P = r'''

**Added 2026-11-13 by the fold of the Edmonton case study:** prompts 9 to 17, for OD-47 to OD-55 (OD-47 to OD-54 are the adjudication's AQ-1 to AQ-8, `scratchpad/session_2026-11-13-edmonton-checklist-pass/ADJUDICATION.md` section 5.3; OD-55 is OQ-T086). Each is written from its register entry; none carries a recommendation, because the adjudicator gave none. Three hold a task's gate (OD-48: T-056 and through it T-115; OD-49: T-091, T-092; OD-53: T-087); the rest hold parts or nothing, as each says.

### 9. OD-47: what lens does a figure carry when its clause names no person, function or need? (holds the parked figures of the Edmonton batch, T-087; bears on T-115 step 3 and T-106)
**Question.** You ruled that a provision under a general disability heading carries no identity, only its ICF and access-need lenses (OD-31), and every figure needs at least one lens. A clause such as "Corridors should be 1100mm" names no one and no function. What lens does it carry?
**Why it is yours.** It decides who a figure is said to be for: the population taxonomy and the lens key.
**Options.** (a) The function the parameter serves, with the parameter's definition as the warrant. *Then* every such figure can be written, and the crossing is held once on the parameter (a schema change). (b) The document's own stated audience. *Then* every item of a document carries the same groups, even items that do not concern them. (c) Not written until a clause names someone; the phrase stays an observation with a gap. *Then* checklists and most code clauses contribute observations only. (d) It keeps `ALL` until you rule per row. *Then* T-115 cannot retire `ALL`.
**Evidence.** `grep -n -F 'OD-31: a provision that names no one' references/project-standards.md`; `grep -n 'def _require_lens_warrant' -A12 scripts/db.py`; `tasks/T-115-retag-all-rows.md` §4 item 2.
**Answer in one line.** `OD-47: function of the parameter` · `OD-47: the document's stated audience` · `OD-47: not written` · `OD-47: keeps ALL until you rule per row`

### 10. OD-48: what does `design_scale = 'universal'` state? (holds T-056, and through it T-115)
**Question.** The engine writes `universal` when a determination rests on codes alone; you ruled that `ALL` leaves the identity lens, "universal being stated once, by design_scale". Today a wheelchair-keyed cell built on codes reads `universal`, and "rests on codes only" is already its own column. Which fact does `design_scale` state?
**Why it is yours.** Your first design-mode rule defines Universal Mode as both "Universal Design" and "Code Compliance".
**Options.** (a) Whom it is for: `universal` when the determination names no identity. *Then* "codes only" is read from its own column, the engine's line changes, and a code-only wheelchair cell reads `population` with the ○ flag. (b) What it rests on, as now. *Then* "for everyone" needs another home and is told apart only by having no identity. (c) Both, as two columns. *Then* a schema change, when one column already exists.
**Evidence.** `grep -n 'design_scale = SCALE_UNIVERSAL' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`; `grep -n -F 'Universal Design / Code Compliance' references/project-standards.md`; `tasks/T-056-all-leaves-identity-lens.md` §4 items 3 and 3a.
**Answer in one line.** `OD-48: whom it is for` · `OD-48: what it rests on` · `OD-48: two columns`

### 11. OD-49: building type, a figure's other circumstances, and where an element lives (holds T-091 and T-092)
**Question.** (a) You ruled three building levels on 2026-08-27 (building types such as residential and commercial, room types, construction elements). None is linked to a figure; building use, new or existing work, and interior or exterior sit together in one free-text cell the engine does not read. Is building type a branch within one determination, part of what a determination is keyed on, or left as it is, and what is its vocabulary? (b) Is the construction-element level a table of its own, or the element terms the catalogue already holds?
**Why it is yours.** Scope vocabulary and the key of a determination (ruled twice); your 2026-08-27 ACTION ("Create three tables") may have been overtaken by OR-14's "typed term pointer".
**Options.** (a1) A typed circumstance on the figure, shown as a branch, with a small vocabulary seeded from your examples and extended by data. *Then* one determination per parameter and lens, with branches. (a2) Part of the key. *Then* one determination per building type, and the key you ruled changes. (a3) Leave it in `setting`. *Then* dwelling and public-building figures compose into one headline, and T-091 and T-092 are declined. (b1) Elements are terms; the third level is derived from them. (b2) A separate `base_elements` table, pointing at or from the term.
**Evidence.** `grep -n -F 'base_building' references/project-standards.md | head -2`; `grep -n -F '13. **OR-14.**' references/project-standards.md`; `tasks/T-091-typed-circumstance-carrier.md` §3 (its command prints the settings).
**Answer in one line.** `OD-49: (a1|a2|a3); (b1|b2)`

### 12. OD-50: may a source that is not a code add a parameter? (holds nothing; bears on T-072 and the Edmonton batch)
**Question.** You ruled that the list of quantities is seeded "From the codes held" (OR-13). The Edmonton checklist, a grey source, states figures for quantities no held parameter takes (handrail height and diameter, stair rise and run, control heights, toilet height, knee space, door dwell time). May such a source promote a parameter, or only mint the term and wait for a code?
**Why it is yours.** It decides what the guidebook's pages can ask about, and on whose word.
**Options.** (a) Any admitted source, in its data pull request, under OR-17's conditions. *Then* the catalogue grows with each reading. (b) Term only; a code or standard must state the quantity. *Then* the terms wait for T-105 and T-072, and stay visible as deferred acts. (c) Term only, promoted when two independent sources state it. *Then* a recurrence rule to build.

- **OD-53 (AQ-7) does hold part of the Edmonton batch.** The adjudicator wrote that it holds nothing. But research gate R16 makes every term named by an adjudication either a parameter or a declined term. So adjudicating `NAMES-EXISTING` to any of the many held terms that are neither turns R16 red unless the batch declines them.
  - I first made OD-53 gate T-087. The replay's report shows it instead adjudicated those observations `DEFERRED`, naming the term and the question, and R16 passed. I switched T-087 to that path, so OD-53 holds part of T-087, not the whole.

T-088 stores only the raw facts and T-089 derives the rest when it reads. My reasons: `dbcore` is stdlib-only and cannot read the stage map, and a stored derivation drifts when the derivation changes (rules 5 and 8).
- **Capture only the running session's calls.** T-088 also captures only calls whose `--session` equals `CURRENT`. Otherwise the tests' deliberate refusals would flood the session record.

- **`term_aliases.alias_type` has no "equivalent".** Its equivalence value is `SYNONYM`; T-029's text says so.
- **The engine's docstring says it reaches only `schemas.*`, but it imports `dbcore`.** T-088 relies on that import.
- **The adjudication cites ledger lines by number.** I checked each cited line and turned it into a `grep -F` in the register entries.
